one_sentence: ISO-019 argues that 8 boundary conditions derived from a Christian-motivated framework uniquely identify Christianity as the only complete worldview.
executive_summary: ISO-019 maps boundary conditions from PDE theory to theological constraints, claiming that 8 conditions (BC1-BC8) are jointly necessary and sufficient for a well-posed worldview. The document asserts that Christianity uniquely satisfies all 8, while other worldviews fail at least one. However, the analysis acknowledges circularity: 3 BCs (Trinity, grace, incarnation) are Christian-presuppositional, undermining the uniqueness claim. The 4 independently derived BCs (self-grounding, conservation, incompleteness, entropy) provide genuine constraint but not uniqueness. The ISO remains a candidate due to this circularity, recommending either independent derivation of the presuppositional BCs or downgrading the claim from 'unique solution' to 'most complete among tested.'
short_summary: ISO-019 is a candidate isomorphism that maps boundary conditions from PDE theory to theological constraints for worldviews. It claims that 8 boundary conditions are jointly necessary and sufficient, with Christianity as the unique solution. Key evidence includes a worldview comparison table showing Christianity scoring 8/8 versus others scoring lower. This matters because it makes the most exclusivist claim in the Theophysics framework, but it is critically weakened by circularity in the selection of boundary conditions.
